ResFormer: spotting atrial fibrillation in ECG

A deep model that reads a single-lead ECG and says whether the rhythm is normal or atrial fibrillation, built by adding attention to a ResNet and giving it the timing between heartbeats.

Code on GitHub (my fork)

The problem

Atrial fibrillation is a heart rhythm disorder that raises stroke risk, and it often comes and goes, so it is easy to miss. Reading ECG strips by hand does not scale, and older classifiers lean on hand-made features.

We compared a CNN-BiLSTM with a ResNet on the PhysioNet 2017 challenge recordings, kept the better ResNet, and added a Transformer-style attention block plus the timing between beats. The aim was to catch long-range structure that convolutions alone can miss.

How it works

  1. Clean the signal.Band-pass filter, resample to 300 Hz, and keep only the Normal and AF classes.
  2. Find the beats.R-peak detection gives the R-R intervals, which carry the irregularity that defines AF.
  3. Waveform branch.A ResNet of 1D residual blocks extracts shape features, then a residual dense block and multi-head attention look across them.
  4. Join and classify.The R-R features are concatenated with the attention output and two dense layers give Normal or AF. Training balances the classes with SMOTETomek.

Results

Normal versus AF on PhysioNet 2017
ModelAccuracySensitivitySpecificity
CNN-BiLSTM87.58%89.33%85.75%
ResNet92.00%90.61%93.31%
ResNet + Transformer (ResFormer)93.25%92.30%94.11%

Source: the research paper summary in the repo. The 0.95 AUROC is from the ICIOT'25 paper itself, which is not in the repo.

Limits and next steps

  • The AF class is the hard one. In the repo's report its precision is 70% and recall 75%, against 96% and 95% for Normal, so the headline accuracy flatters the minority class.
  • Two classes only. The challenge's "Other" class is dropped, which makes this easier than the full task.
  • One dataset, one random split and no external validation. The gain over ResNet is 1.25 points, and I have no confidence interval for it.
  • The repo's own conclusion names the next step: deal with the class imbalance and raise sensitivity before this could matter clinically.
